title: Projection omitting one coordinate
statement: Let $\Omega$ be a finite set with probability mass function $\pi$, let $n$ be a natural number, let $i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}$, and let $f:\Omega^n\to\mathbb R$. The coordinate projection of $f$ at $i$ is its projection onto all coordinates other than $i$, obtained by averaging over the product distribution while retaining the input on those other coordinates.
hypotheses_covered: $\pi$ is a probability mass function on $\Omega$
